skill.name: claude-chrome
skill.description: Browser automation guidance for controlling a logged-in Chrome session with Claude Code, the Claude in Chrome extension, or Chrome DevTools MCP.
skill.summary: Use Claude to automate Chrome navigation, form filling, debugging, data extraction, and recurring browser workflows.
skill.author: Dicklesworthstone

security_audit.summary: Most static external-command hits are Markdown code fences, inline tool names, or user prompt examples rather than executable Ruby backticks. The real risks are unpinned npx-based MCP setup, browser screenshot capture, authenticated session control, scheduled automation, and file upload capability. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed skill file.

remediation.issue: Unpinned MCP package execution through npx
remediation.suggestion: Pin chrome-devtools-mcp to a reviewed version and document that users should install it only from trusted package sources.

remediation.issue: Authenticated browser automation can access sensitive accounts
remediation.suggestion: Require narrow site allowlists, explicit confirmations for account actions, and clear guidance for handling private data.

remediation.issue: Screenshot and DOM capture may expose private page content
remediation.suggestion: Warn users before captures on sensitive sites and recommend redaction or exclusion of credentials, tokens, and personal data.

remediation.issue: Scheduled browser tasks can run later without active supervision
remediation.suggestion: Limit scheduled tasks to low-risk workflows and require review before sending messages, publishing, purchasing, or sharing data.

semantic_findings.title: Authenticated Browser Session Access
semantic_findings.description: The skill states that Claude can use the real Chrome session and interact with logged-in services such as Gmail, Google Docs, Notion, and CRMs. This can expose private data or perform account actions if permissions and confirmations are too broad.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file explicitly describes using existing browser login state and names sensitive authenticated services. The risk follows directly from the intended browser automation model.

semantic_findings.title: Recurring Browser Automation Requires Tight Scope
semantic_findings.description: The skill describes scheduled browser tasks that run automatically with notifications. Recurring automation against email, competitor sites, or expense systems can create delayed data access or account-action risk without careful review gates.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The scheduled-task feature and examples are stated directly. The presence of notifications reduces but does not remove the risk of broad recurring automation.

semantic_findings.title: Browser File Upload Capability
semantic_findings.description: The DevTools MCP tool list includes upload_file, and the workflow examples include forms that use company documents. This can move local files into web applications and needs explicit user approval.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The upload tool and document-backed form workflow are both explicit. The finding is contextual because the static scanner only classified the inline tool name as external command text.

content.value_statement: Manual browser tasks slow down testing, data entry, and routine research. This skill shows how Claude, Codex, and Claude Code can control Chrome through the Anthropic extension or Chrome DevTools MCP.
actual_capabilities: Explains setup for Claude Code with the Claude in Chrome extension.
Shows how to connect Chrome DevTools MCP using npx or MCP configuration.
Lists browser actions such as navigation, clicks, form filling, and tab management.
Covers screenshots, DOM snapshots, console logs, network requests, and performance traces.
Provides examples for local testing, Gmail, Google Docs, Notion, CRMs, and reports.
Describes workflow shortcuts, multi-tab work, and scheduled browser tasks.
limitations: Requires Google Chrome, Claude Code, the Chrome extension, and a paid Claude plan.
The extension does not support Brave, Arc, Edge, WSL, or mobile devices.
Authenticated automation can expose sensitive account data if site access is too broad.
Chrome extension mode is not headless; headless support applies only to DevTools MCP.

use_cases.title: Test Web Applications
use_cases.description: Run browser flows against localhost, check validation messages, inspect console errors, and capture screenshots for bugs.

use_cases.title: Automate Data Entry
use_cases.description: Fill repeated CRM or vendor forms from approved source data while pausing before final submission.

use_cases.title: Collect Authenticated Reports
use_cases.description: Open logged-in dashboards, extract summary data, and prepare concise reports from approved business systems.

prompt_templates.title: Open And Inspect Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Open the target page in a new Chrome tab, summarize the visible content, and list any obvious page errors.

prompt_templates.title: Test A Form Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Open localhost:3000, submit the login form with invalid data, verify validation messages, and report any console errors.

prompt_templates.title: Extract Approved Data
prompt_templates.prompt: Open the approved dashboard, extract this week's totals, verify the values on screen, and summarize the result in a table.

prompt_templates.title: Design A Scheduled Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a weekly browser workflow that checks approved pages, records changes, and pauses before sending or publishing anything.

output_examples.input: Test the checkout flow and check for browser errors.
output_examples.output: A short test report with completed steps, observed validation behavior, console errors, screenshots taken, and issues needing manual review.

output_examples.input: Collect this week's traffic summary from an approved dashboard.
output_examples.output: A concise summary of visits, sources, notable changes, and the page where each value was verified.

output_examples.input: Prepare drafts for unread engineering emails without sending them.
output_examples.output: A list of drafted reply summaries, recipients, and confirmation prompts before any message is sent.

best_practices: Use narrow site permissions and confirm before publishing, purchasing, sending, or sharing data.
Write specific prompts with expected pages, success criteria, and verification steps.
Pause at CAPTCHAs, login prompts, modal dialogs, and any unexpected account action.
anti_patterns: Do not grant broad access to personal or work accounts without task limits.
Do not automate financial actions, purchases, publishing, or data sharing without explicit review.
Do not install unpinned MCP packages in sensitive or regulated environments.

faq.question: Does this skill control my real Chrome browser?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes using Chrome with your current login state through the extension or DevTools MCP.

faq.question: Can it work behind logins?
faq.answer: Yes, when Chrome already has an authenticated session and site permissions allow access.

faq.question: Does it support Chrome DevTools MCP?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill documents MCP installation, configuration, and the available browser automation tools.

faq.question: Can it run scheduled tasks?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill describes recurring shortcuts for daily, weekly, monthly, or annual browser workflows.

faq.question: What should users review before automation runs?
faq.answer: Users should review site permissions, sensitive data exposure, file uploads, and any action that sends or publishes information.

faq.question: What environments are not supported?
faq.answer: The extension does not support other Chromium browsers, WSL, mobile devices, or headless Chrome extension mode.
